FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 5 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 14 September 1988, after the draft finalized by the Medical Glass Instruments and Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. This part ( part 5 ) is one of a series of methods of test for assessing the biological hazards of medical devices that directly come in contact with body tissues or of substances that are to be introduced in the body by means other than oral. This standard is proposed to be published in 12 parts. Part 1 Part 2 Part 3 Part 4 Part 6 Part 7 Part 8 Part 9 Part 10 Terminology Selection of biological methods of test Method of testing by tissue implantation Method of test for systemic toxicity: Assessment of acute toxicity of extracts from medical devices Method of test for systemic toxicity: Assessment of pyrogenicity in rabbits of extracts from medical devices Methods of test for sensitization: Assessment of potential of medical devices to produce delayed contact dermatitis Methods of test for skin irritation of extracts from medical devices Method of test for skin irritation of solid medical devices Method of test for dental materials Other parts are as follows:

Part I1 Method of test for eye irritation Part 12 Methods of test for toxicity to CdS in CdtUre of extracts from medical devices part 2 of this standard provides guidance On the selection of recommended methods of test fo, the initial assessment of biological hazards In medal devices which has been referred to in this part ( Part 5 ) of the standard. ln the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from BS 5736 : part 4 : 1981 `Evaluation of medical devices for biological hazards; Part 4 Method of' test for intr;IcuLaneous reactivity of extracts from medical devices', issued by the British Standards Institution, UK.

PART 5 METHOD OF TEST FOR INTRACUTANEOUS REACTIVITY OF EXTRACTS FROM MEDICAL DEVICES 1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes a method of test designed to assess the localized reaction of tissue to leachable inherent or extraneous substances present in or on a medical device. 1.2 The method specifies use of a polar and nonpolar solvent to obtain extracts that are administercd as intracutaneous injections to rabbits and assessed for intracutaneous reactivity after injection at 94, 48 and 72 h thereafter. 1.3 The method of test is recommended for the initial assessment of devices in Categories A, BI, C and El ( see IS 12572 ( Part 2 ) : 1988, Category A - Thse devices intended for long-term ( long-term covers a period from a few months to permanent use ) implantation within the body tissue, for example, artery grafts and hip prostheses; Category B, - Those devices intended for long-term ( long-term covers a period from a few months to permanent use ) or repeated contact with mucosal surfilces, for example, contraceptive dcviccs: Category C - Those devices intended for short-term ( short-term covers a period from a few minutes to several weeks continuous use ) use within the body or in contact with mucosal surfaces, for example, tracheal tubes, urinary catheters and intravenous cannulae; and C'utegoq~ El --~ Those devices intended to contain or administer substances including blood, that are introduced parenterally into the body, for example, blood bags, haemodi;tlysic intravenous equipment, administration sets and kits and hypoderm~c syringes. 2 DEFINITION~S For Ihc purpose of this standard. the following tletinilions shall appl!,. 2.1 Erythema Tissue reaction characterized by redness at the injection site. 2.2 Eschar Kcaction characterized by scab formation. 2.3 Final Product Medical device in its ruadb,-for-use state. 2.4 Injection Site The site of injection and 5 mm tissue surrounding the puncture.2.5 Intracutaneous Injection Injection into the skin tissues. 2.6 Iatracotaneous Reactivity Undesirable effect(s). typically erythema or oedema which become apparent within 72 h of administration of an extract or extractant by intracutaneous injection. 2.7 Medical Device
Any item used in medical treatment, diagrlosis or contraception, not intended to have a pharm~~_ logical action on the body.

2.8 Ocdema T i s s u e reaction charactcriLed by swelling at the injection site. 2.9 Test Material The final product or sample of final product that is to bc tcstcd. 3 ANIMALS AND HUSl3ANDRY 3.1 Four albino rabbits of a sitlgle str',lin, weighing not less than 2 kg each, sha!l tx used.

6 PRESENTATION OF RESULTS The results shall be submitted in a test report that includes a complete record of the method o f extraction and procedures followed, and any other relevant data necessary for the assessment of results as described in 7. 7 ASSESSMENT OF RESULTS

7.1 The assessment of the result should be carried o u t b y a n expcricnced p e r s o n ( preferably a toxicologist ) who is aware of the conditions of use of the final product and has wirh him appropriate chemical and biological data concernitlg it ( see 3.3 and 3.4 of IS 12572 ( Part 2 ) : 1988 7.2 The overall assessment of the test results shall be done, taking into consideration any diffcrencc observed between the mean numerical I.ating of an extract and the mean numerical rating of' its extractant and all other information in the test report. 7.3 If the assessor ( toxicologist ) considers the results to be either inconclusive or invalid, the test shall be repeated using different animals, fresh extracts and if necessary, fresh extractant. 7.3.1 The non-polar solvent may produce a posi.tive numerical rating. This need not invalidate the test. 7.4 The result of the assessment shall be recorded in the test report.
